solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Complete flunkey in power

blocks.note: to do a job is to complete it
a minion is a servile follower, a flunkey

explanation.surface: A lackey fully installed in the corridors of power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complete' looks like an adjective qualifying the flunkey, but it is a verb: to do something is to complete it.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominion means sovereign authority or rule over territory, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Lower seabed is churned up

indicators.note: sand churned up by waves is stirred into disorder, so the letters of the seabed are scrambled

blocks.note: anagram fodder, six letters

explanation.surface: A dredger or storm stirs up the ocean floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower' reads like a comparative adjective describing the seabed; it is a verb, and the fodder sits right beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To debase something is to reduce its quality or value, to degrade it.

clue.text: Presbyterian minister married toreador, unwisely

indicators.note: doing something unwisely means doing it badly or wrongly, so the letters of toreador end up wrongly placed

blocks.note: M is the standard abbreviation for married
anagram fodder, eight letters

explanation.surface: A churchman scandalously weds a bullfighter.
explanation.walkthrough: In Presbyterian churches such as the Church of Scotland, the Moderator is the minister who chairs a church court or the General Assembly.
explanation.definitionFit: The title Moderator names the presiding cleric of a Presbyterian assembly, so it is a specific office held by such a clergyman.

clue.text: Originally called vacuous dandy insecure

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so the word beside it loses its contents and keeps only its outside

blocks.note: née, used for a woman's name at birth, means originally called
dandy emptied of its middle leaves its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A shallow fop, as he used to be known, has always been unsure of himself.
explanation.walkthrough: Née, French for born, introduces a maiden name, which is why it can stand for 'originally called'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone emotionally needy craves reassurance, so an insecure person fits this informal sense.

clue.text: Company about to discharge army swimmer

indicators.note: turning about means facing the other way, so the company's abbreviation is read backwards

blocks.note: CO is the abbreviation for company
used literally
pus is the discharge from an infected wound

explanation.surface: A regiment is about to release a soldier who swims.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discharge army' looks like a military phrase, but 'army' belongs to the definition: a creature with eight arms is 'army' in the sense of well supplied with arms.
explanation.definitionFit: This sea creature has eight arms, so the coined adjective humorously describes a many-limbed marine animal.

clue.text: Part of Vita’s garden is heaven for northerners

indicators.note: only a portion of the following words is wanted, a run of letters inside them

blocks.note: the letters run across the apostrophe and into the next word

explanation.surface: Vita Sackville-West's famous garden at Sissinghurst is paradise to visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: Vita Sackville-West created the celebrated garden at Sissinghurst in Kent; the answer spans vitA'S GARDen.
explanation.definitionFit: In Norse mythology the gods live in this realm, so Scandinavians of old regarded it as their celestial home.

clue.text: Novel in store at WH Smith?

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters that follow are made into something new

blocks.note: anagram fodder, nine letters

explanation.surface: A shopper asks whether some book is available at the high-street chain.
explanation.walkthrough: WH Smith is a British chain selling newspapers, books, pens and paper; the question mark marks it as an example. 'Novel' looks like a book on the shelf and is the anagram indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: The chain is a well-known example of a shop selling writing materials, so the definition works by example.

clue.text: Silver and gold accepted in marketplace

blocks.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
or is gold in heraldry
A is an abbreviation for accepted, as on a bill of exchange

explanation.surface: Precious metals are taken as payment at the market.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'and' simply joins the first two pieces, and 'accepted' gives its abbreviation rather than containing anything.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greek cities the agora was the public square where traders gathered, a historical synonym.

clue.text: Lovely First Lady will ultimately mess up

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the word before it is kept

blocks.note: an attractive person is informally a dish
Eve was the first woman in Genesis
the last letter of wilL

explanation.surface: A beautiful president's wife is going to ruin something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First Lady' suggests a president's wife, but here it is the first woman of all; 'Lovely' is an adjective turned into a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To dishevel hair or clothes is to make them untidy or rumpled, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Spooner’s father gambles money that won’t be repaid

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so the phrase must have its initial sounds exchanged

blocks.note: an informal word for father, which takes the B sound from the next word
to bet is to gamble; this word takes the D sound from the first

explanation.surface: Dad keeps betting, and the money he borrows will never come back.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening consonants of DAD BETS and you get BAD DEBTS; the surface neatly explains why the money is lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Accountants write off loans that creditors cannot recover, and those uncollectable sums are called by this phrase.

clue.text: Cheers state alcohol bans

indicators.note: to state something is to say it, so the following word is heard rather than spelt

blocks.note: ta is British slang for thanks
booze is slang for alcohol

explanation.surface: A government prohibits drinking, in a nod to the toast 'Cheers'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheers' looks like a toast, but British speakers also use it, like ta, to mean thanks. 'State' looks like a government and is the sound signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Taboos are social or religious prohibitions, so the plural noun matches the noun sense of the word.

clue.text: Boss sobs, denying every small blunder

indicators.note: denying means refusing or withholding, and every means all occurrences are removed from the words before it

blocks.note: the two words written together
S is the standard abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: An employer weeps over a minor mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip all four of the S's from BOSS SOBS and the letters left read B,O,O,B.
explanation.definitionFit: A boob is British informal slang for a silly mistake or gaffe.

clue.text: Random fish on street

blocks.note: St is the abbreviation for street
a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: A fish turns up by chance in the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' marks position: the fish comes after the street in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A stray bullet or remark is one that is accidental or haphazard, an adjectival synonym.

clue.text: Closest friend follows professional team

indicators.note: to follow is to come after, so the friend is placed after the professional team in the answer

blocks.note: a pro is a professional
a cricket or football team is an eleven, XI in Roman numerals
mate is informal for friend

explanation.surface: Your best friend supports a professional side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Closest friend' reads as one phrase, but the definition is 'Closest' alone and the friend comes last in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Proximate means nearest in space, time or causation, a formal synonym.

clue.text: Inactivity of MI6 station coming to the fore

indicators.note: coming to the fore means moving to the front, so the station's piece goes before the intelligence service's

blocks.note: Sta. is the abbreviation for station
MI6 is the Secret Intelligence Service

explanation.surface: A British spy outpost has gone quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: MI6 is Britain's foreign intelligence agency, officially the SIS; the clue order puts it first, so the station must be moved in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Stasis is a state of equilibrium where nothing changes or develops, matching a lack of activity.

clue.text: North America shuns Finnish PM over enclave

indicators.note: to shun is to avoid or keep away, so the continent's two letters are kept out of the name

blocks.note: NA is the abbreviation for North America
Sanna Marin was Prime Minister of Finland from 2019 to 2023
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A diplomatic snub: the US and Canada cold-shoulder Finland's leader over some territory.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove NA from SANNA MARIN and add O. Many readers will not have the Finnish leader's full name to hand, which is the key.
explanation.definitionFit: This tiny republic lies entirely surrounded by Italian territory, which is exactly what an enclave is.

clue.text: Female dons curse female spirit

indicators.note: to don is to put on clothing, so the woman is wrapped inside the curse

blocks.note: a bane is a curse or source of ruin
she is the female pronoun

explanation.surface: A woman puts a hex on someone and becomes a supernatural being.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dons' reads as if the woman wears the curse, but putting on clothing means being wrapped by it, so the curse goes round her. 'Female' appears twice: once as wordplay, once in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In Irish folklore this wailing ghostly woman foretells a death in the family.

clue.text: Gibbon, perhaps? Wrong – it’s a rhino

indicators.note: something wrong is incorrect, so the letters after it are in the incorrect order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, nine letters

explanation.surface: Someone misidentifies an ape at the zoo: that is no gibbon, it is a rhino.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gibbon' suggests the ape, but it is Edward Gibbon, author of The Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire; 'perhaps' marks him as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Gibbon wrote a celebrated account of Rome's fall, so he is an example of a scholar of the past.

clue.text: Excuses girl and boy pinching one shilling

indicators.note: pinching means grabbing and holding, so the boy's word holds the number inside it

blocks.note: a girl's name
a son is a boy
I is the Roman numeral one
s was the abbreviation for a shilling

explanation.surface: Two children who stole a coin make up stories to get off.
explanation.walkthrough: A shilling was a pre-decimal British coin, abbreviated s. The boy holds the one (S-I-ON) and the shilling goes on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Evasions are dodges and prevarications used to avoid answering, which is close to excuses.

clue.text: Gallery and museum welcoming monarch

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so the museum's letters take in the monarch

blocks.note: the V&A, Victoria and Albert Museum in London, written out
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: An art gallery and a museum host a royal visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gallery and museum' looks like two cultural venues, but 'Gallery' is the definition. The V&A is London's Victoria and Albert Museum, spelt out as V AND A.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallery can mean a roofed platform or porch along the outside of a building, the same thing as a veranda.

clue.text: Like taking clothes off

indicators.note: taking off clothes removes the outer layer, so the word before loses its outside letters

blocks.note: tAKINg without its outer letters

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys undressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like' reads as a verb, to enjoy; it is the preposition or adjective meaning similar.
explanation.definitionFit: Akin means related or similar in character, which matches the adjective sense of alike.

clue.text: Frightful female pair refused to go on

indicators.note: what is refused is turned away, so the two letters for a pair are sent off from the next word

blocks.note: to progress is to go on, advance
pr is an abbreviation for pair

explanation.surface: Two awful women will not carry on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pair refused' reads as two people declining, but the pair is PR, dropped from PROGRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogress is a female ogre, a monstrous and terrifying woman of folklore.

clue.text: Old ass pulled up herb

indicators.note: in a down clue, pulling something up turns it bottom to top, so the animal is read backwards

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
an onager is a wild ass of Asia

explanation.surface: An elderly donkey tugs a herb out of the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The onager is a crossword favourite for 'ass'; 'pulled up' fits the surface of a plant being uprooted.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregano is a fragrant culinary plant of the mint family, a type of herb.

clue.text: Picked nose rudely after church

indicators.note: doing something rudely means doing it roughly, so the letters of the nose are roughly rearranged

blocks.note: CH is the abbreviation for church
anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A worshipper has a bad habit after the service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked nose' reads as one act, but 'Picked' is the definition, a past participle meaning selected.
explanation.definitionFit: Chosen and picked are both past participles meaning selected from among options.

clue.text: Lacking energy, Sue and mum tucked into pickle sandwich

indicators.note: lacking means without, so the name loses the letter for energy
to be tucked into something is to be put inside it, so mother goes into the pickle

blocks.note: SUE with its E, for energy, deleted
brine is salty pickling liquid
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A tired mother and daughter eat a sandwich with pickle in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pickle' is the food in the surface and brine in the wordplay; mum goes in after the B.
explanation.definitionFit: A submarine, or sub, is a long bread roll filled with meat and cheese, chiefly an American name.

clue.text: Staff keep getting the runs

blocks.note: a short stick, as carried by a conductor or police officer
in cricket, a batter who keeps scoring runs carries on at the crease

explanation.surface: Employees keep suffering from diarrhoea.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits as BAT ON: to bat on is to go on batting in cricket, where runs are the points scored.
explanation.definitionFit: A baton is a rod or stick, and a staff is likewise a stick, while to bat on is to continue scoring in cricket.

clue.text: Very discontented Turkish canine?

indicators.note: discontented is read as dis-content-ed, with its content removed, so the word keeps only its outside letters

blocks.note: too means very, excessively
Turkish emptied of its contents leaves T and H

explanation.surface: A very unhappy Turkish dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canine' suggests a dog, but it is also a pointed tooth; the question mark flags the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A canine is one of the four pointed teeth between the incisors and premolars, an example.

clue.text: Reportedly followed plot

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is told, so the word that follows is to be heard rather than read

blocks.note: to track someone is to follow them

explanation.surface: A conspiracy that someone has been told about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' first suggests a conspiracy; here it is a piece of land.
explanation.definitionFit: A tract is an area of land, and so is a plot, though a tract is usually larger.

clue.text: Get the better of guy after university

blocks.note: the OU is the Open University, Britain's distance-learning university
to guy someone is to mock them, and to twit is to tease

explanation.surface: Someone beats a man who has just left college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a noun for a man, but it is a verb: to guy is to ridicule, and to twit is to taunt. The OU is the Open University.
explanation.definitionFit: To outwit someone is to defeat them by greater cleverness, the same as besting them.

clue.text: Fancies retiring, a very good sign

indicators.note: to retire is to withdraw into somewhere, so the article withdraws inside the abbreviation

blocks.note: VG is the abbreviation for very good, as a teacher writes
used literally
Aries is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A shy person's whims are taken as a promising omen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' reads as shy; it tells the A to withdraw inside VG.
explanation.definitionFit: Vagaries are whims or capricious notions, which is one sense of the plural noun fancies.

clue.text: I snore violently, being older

indicators.note: something shaken violently is thrown into disorder, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: anagram fodder, six letters

explanation.surface: An old person admits to snoring loudly now they have aged.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder and the definition sit in one convincing confession, which is why the letters of 'I snore' are easy to overlook.
explanation.definitionFit: Senior means higher in age or rank, a comparative-style adjective like the definition.

clue.text: Order revolutionary books and articles from Helena?

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the order's two letters are turned back to front

blocks.note: OM is the Order of Merit
NT is the New Testament, a set of books
an is an indefinite article, used twice

explanation.surface: A command that radical literature and newspaper pieces be sent over from someone named Helena.
explanation.walkthrough: Helena looks like a woman's name, but it is the state capital of Montana; the question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone living in Helena is a resident of that northwestern American state, since the city is its capital.
